q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'LACONIC'.
e: Laconic means using very few words, so the nearest meaning is Concise.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'EPHEMERAL'.
e: Ephemeral means lasting only a very short time; its opposite is Permanent.

q: What does the idiom 'to let sleeping dogs lie' mean?
o: To avoid reviving an old trouble
e: The idiom means: To avoid reviving an old trouble, that is, leave a settled issue alone.

q: Choose the one word for: a speech delivered without any previous preparation.
e: A speech given on the spot without preparation is called Extempore.

q: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: 'Neither the manager / nor his assistants / was present / at the meeting.'
e: The error is in 'was present': with neither/nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'assistants', which is plural, so it should be 'were present'.

q: Choose the correct passive form of: 'Who wrote this letter?'
o: By whom was this letter written?
By whom this letter was written?
By whom has this letter been written?
e: A 'Who' question in simple past becomes 'By whom was this letter written?' in the passive, keeping the question word order and past tense.

q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said to me, "Have you finished your homework?"
o: He asked me had I finished my homework.
He asked me if I had finished my homework.
He asked me if I have finished my homework.
He said to me that I had finished my homework.
e: A yes/no question uses 'asked' with 'if', statement word order, and present perfect shifts to past perfect: He asked me if I had finished my homework.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The clerk was accused ___ theft.
e: The verb 'accuse' takes the preposition 'of': accused of theft.

o: She likes to swim, reading and dancing.
She likes swimming, reading and dancing.
She likes swimming, reading and to dance.
She likes swim, read and dancing.
e: Items in a list should share the same form; three gerunds give: She likes swimming, reading and dancing.

q: Choose the sentence that is free from a dangling modifier.
o: Walking along the beach, a shell caught my eye.
Walking along the beach, the shell was noticed by me.
While walking along the beach, a shell caught my eye.
Walking along the beach, I noticed a shell.
e: The opening phrase must refer to the person walking, who must be the subject: Walking along the beach, I noticed a shell.

q: Fill in the blank: The new rule will not ___ students who joined last year.
e: The verb meaning 'to influence or change' is 'affect', so the rule will not affect the students.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'OBSEQUIOUS'.
e: Obsequious means excessively eager to please or obey, which is Servile.
